output_text:
name: python-observability
description: Python structured logging, metrics, tracing, and production debugging.

Use for logging, Prometheus metrics, distributed tracing, correlation IDs, dashboards, and production debugging. Enable answering “what, where, and why” without deploying new code.

Principles:
- Emit JSON logs in production with consistent fields; consider human-readable logs locally.
- Track latency, traffic, errors, and saturation at every service boundary.
- Generate a unique ID at ingress and propagate it through logs, spans, and outbound requests.
- Keep metric label values bounded. Unbounded labels (like user IDs) explode storage costs.
- Avoid labels with unbounded values to prevent metric explosion.
- Never log expected behavior at `ERROR`. A user entering a wrong password is `INFO`, not `ERROR`.

Logging: Configure `structlog` with `merge_contextvars`, `add_log_level`, `TimeStamper(fmt="iso")`, `StackInfoRenderer`, `format_exc_info`, `JSONRenderer`, `make_filtering_bound_logger`, `PrintLoggerFactory`, and `cache_logger_on_first_use=True`. Use `structlog.get_logger()`. Include correlation ID, method, path, user ID, duration, result, and error type/message where relevant. Levels: `DEBUG` diagnostics; `INFO` lifecycle/operations; `WARNING` recoverable anomalies; `ERROR` failures needing attention.

Correlation: Use `contextvars.ContextVar` and `structlog.contextvars.bind_contextvars`. FastAPI middleware reads `X-Correlation-ID` or creates `str(uuid.uuid4())`, sets it, and returns it in the response header. Send it on outbound `httpx.AsyncClient` requests as `headers={"X-Correlation-ID": correlation_id.get()}`.

Metrics: Use `prometheus_client.Counter`, `Histogram`, and `Gauge`. Track request latency (`http_request_duration_seconds`), requests (`http_requests_total`), errors (`http_errors_total`), and DB pool usage (`db_connection_pool_used`). Request labels may include method, endpoint, status; errors may include error_type.
`REQUEST_COUNT.labels(method="GET", user_id=user.id)  # Don't do this!`
Use bounded labels, e.g. `method="GET", endpoint="/users", status="200"` or bounded `user_tier`.

Use `time.perf_counter()` and a reusable `contextmanager` for operation timing; log start, elapsed milliseconds, and errors.

Tracing: Use OpenTelemetry (`opentelemetry`, `TracerProvider`, `BatchSpanProcessor`, `OTLPSpanExporter`); configure a provider/exporter and instrument nested spans with attributes. See https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/python/ for current API patterns.

Best practices: structured logs; propagate correlation IDs; track the four golden signals; bound label cardinality; use appropriate log levels; include context; use context managers; separate observability from business logic; test logs and metrics in integration tests; set up alerts.
